Positioning

Why my background creates stronger SEO audits.

My background is not traditional SEO. I started in finance and accounting, then moved into process automation, data engineering, analytics, and growth. That path shaped the way I approach technical SEO: I look at websites as systems.

A page may have good copy but still fail because it loads slowly, is poorly linked, has weak metadata, renders important content through JavaScript, lacks structured data, or does not clearly answer the questions users and AI systems need answered.

This is where my analytical background becomes useful. I can inspect HTML and JavaScript, review analytics events, analyze funnels, identify page experience problems, and turn technical findings into clear recommendations for business teams, marketers, and developers.

Customer value

Focused on the issues that block visibility and revenue.

The goal is not to produce a long report. The goal is to identify what blocks search visibility, AI discoverability, page experience, and conversion performance — then prioritize what to fix first.

Audit principle

Technical diagnosis

I inspect how pages are built, rendered, linked, indexed, and measured, so recommendations are based on evidence rather than generic SEO checklists.

Audit principle

Analytics-led prioritization

I connect SEO issues to user behavior, funnel drop-offs, conversion paths, and business impact, helping teams focus on the fixes that matter first.

Audit principle

AI visibility readiness

I help structure pages so search engines and AI-powered systems can understand the topic, entity, intent, and useful answers behind the content.

Areas of expertise

Technical SEO, analytics, and AI visibility in one workflow.

I combine technical inspection, user behavior analysis, and structured content thinking so SEO recommendations are grounded in how websites actually work and how users actually behave.
